study: Does a published meta-analysis pool the trial's PRE-REGISTERED primary? (headline study)
data: metadat R package NCT-linked MAs (open source; trial->NCT links CURATED, so linkage FP ~0). Only 3 metadat MAs carry NCTs; only axfors2021 has enough (23) to measure.

axfors2021.review: Axfors 2021, mortality with HCQ/CQ in COVID-19 (a DELIBERATELY mortality-specific pooled analysis)
axfors2021.timepoint_switch: n/a (mortality has no timepoint variants here)
axfors2021.hand_verified: 22/23 classifications correct on inspection (1 MATCH borderline: NCT04261517 shows virological primaries)

conclusion_flip_test: UNDEFINED for this trial set — the 23 trials registered ~23 DIFFERENT primaries, so one cannot 'pool the registered primary' across them. You must pick an outcome (mortality); then most trials measured it as a secondary. This is a BOUNDARY CONDITION of the 'pool the pre-registered primary' prescription.
matcher_fp: trial->NCT linkage FP ~0 (metadat-curated); outcome classification hand-verified + cross-vendored
cross_vendor: agy/Gemini: Q1 BENIGN-OUTCOME-SPECIFIC (not switching evidence); Q2 NO-HETEROGENEOUS-PRIMARIES (prescription inapplicable to this trial set).
verdict: HEADLINE REFUTED / QUALIFIED (reported per pre-registration). The raw '35% primary / 65% non-primary' is NOT evidence of QRP outcome-switching-inheritance — it is the BENIGN, by-design behaviour of an outcome-specific (mortality) meta-analysis, cross-vendor confirmed. Reporting it as switching would be the 'wanting the result' trap.
what_survives: 1) The clean QRP outcome-switching signal is the TRIAL-LEVEL measurement (registry primary vs the primary the PAPER reported) = 6.1% confirmed (OUTCOME_SWITCHING.md); registry-first IS structurally immune to THAT. 2) Registry-first makes the per-trial registration status of a pooled outcome VISIBLE (35% primary / 35% secondary / 30% unregistered) — a transparency/confidence annotation for GRADE, not a 'we catch cheating' claim. 3) Boundary: 'pool the pre-registered primary' is inapplicable when trials register heterogeneous primaries.
named_blocker: Scale needs pairwise70 (374 reviews + included NCTs; local_beae89ce) — NOT in tree (metadat gives only 1 usable NCT-linked MA). Distinguishing benign-outcome-specific from QRP-inherited switching needs the paper-reported-primary layer (the 6.1% trial-level measurement).
